sections.h2: Where is Jasper County, SC, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Jasper County is the southernmost county in South Carolina, in the Lowcountry, with Ridgeland as the county seat and Hardeeville as the largest community. It covers 701.58 square miles, of which 46.42 are water, and it borders Hampton and Beaufort counties in South Carolina and Chatham and Effingham counties in Georgia.

The county was formed in 1912 from parts of Hampton and Beaufort counties. For decades it was one of the poorer counties in the state. Growth since 2000 brought new residents and a larger tax base. The population was 20,678 in 2000 and 28,791 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 38,533.

The Savannah River, the Intracoastal Waterway and several tidal rivers run through or along the county. If your house sits near water, ask your insurance agent and the county planning office about flood zone status; we did not find a flood map on the county pages we opened.

sections.h2: Who sends and collects property tax in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Three county offices share the work: the Assessor sets value and takes appeals, the Auditor prepares bills and handles vehicles, and the Treasurer collects payment. Past-due taxes move to the Delinquent Tax Collector.

The county Treasurer page says real property questions go to the Assessor, vehicle tax notices for a car you no longer own go to the Auditor, and past-due taxes go to the Tax Collector's Office. All sit in the government building at 358 Third Avenue in Ridgeland.

sections.h2: When are Jasper County property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Jasper County posts January 15 as the last day to pay without penalty. For 2026 taxes paid in 2027 the Treasurer lists these dates:

Pay byPenalty startsTotal penalty
January 15, 2027January 16, 20273%
February 1, 2027February 2, 202710%
March 16, 2027March 17, 202715%

After March 17, tax files go to the Delinquent Tax Collector. State law sets the structure: a first penalty, then added percentages on February 2 and March 17, and an execution after that. The statute also lets the treasurer waive a penalty if a mailed payment was wrongly postmarked, and requires a waiver in one case: the property changed hands, the bill went to the old owner, and the new owner got no timely notice. Read Section 12-45-180 for the wording.

The county page we opened does not list payment methods, so call the Treasurer to confirm how you can pay.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent real property taxes in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Delinquent real property in Jasper County can end up at a tax sale, and the owner then has 12 months to redeem. The county's real property collection page lays out this timeline under Section 12-51-40:

  • March 17: taxes become delinquent.
  • April 1: delinquent notices are mailed.
  • Usually September: certified notices go out for delinquent real estate and mobile homes.
  • Three consecutive Wednesdays before the sale: the county advertises the properties in a local paper.
  • First Monday of November: the sale takes place at the Clementa C. Pinckney Government Building, 358 Third Avenue, Ridgeland.

After the sale, the owner, a mortgage company or a grantee can pay the taxes and sale costs within 12 months from the sale date to take the property back. For a seller, that clock is a deadline for any plan to save the house or sell it. Selling before the first Monday of November lets the back taxes be paid out of the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Jasper County property assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal in writing, starting with the Assessor, and the first deadline is 90 days after the assessment notice was mailed. Jasper County lays out the steps on its Assessor Appeals page, and they follow Sections 12-60-2510 to 12-60-2550 of the state code.

  1. Ask the Assessor in writing for a meeting. The conference is set within about 30 days, and missing it waives further appeal for that year.
  2. If the issue is not settled, file a written protest within 30 days of the conference or the Assessor's Notice of Action. Include your name, address, phone, a description of the property, your reasons, and the value and classification you believe are correct.
  3. The Assessor responds in writing, usually within about 30 days.
  4. Appeal to the county Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days of that response, or the new value becomes final.
  5. Exchange evidence at least 15 days before the Board conference, and file replies at least 7 days before.
  6. Request a contested case hearing at the Administrative Law Court within 30 days of the Board's written decision.

In years with no assessment notice, you can appeal at any time. An appeal filed before January 15 counts for that tax year, and one filed on or after January 15 counts for the next. Only authorized persons may act for an owner, such as an attorney, CPA, fiduciary or appraiser, and the authorization must name a specific individual.

If the appeal is not finished by December 31, state law has the assessor tell the auditor to bill at 80 percent of the protested amount, then true up later with interest.

sections.h2: How does the 4 percent legal residence rate work in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Under South Carolina law, an owner-occupied legal residence and up to five contiguous acres are taxed on 4 percent of fair market value. Owners must apply on or before the first penalty date for the first year they claim it, and the home cannot be rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year.

Claiming the rate when you do not qualify carries a penalty of 100 percent of the tax paid plus interest. Jasper County also has a page for reporting residential exemption fraud. Agricultural land can qualify for a 4 percent rate too, but changing the land to another use triggers rollback taxes for the current year and the three before it. Jasper County lists agricultural qualifications on its Taxes page, and the statewide rules are in Chapter 43 of Title 12.

Values are revisited every fifth year, and owners must be told about any change of $1,000 or more. A county can postpone new values by one tax year by ordinance. Ask the Assessor which year Jasper County is on.

sections.h2: What should a Jasper County seller know about growth, roads and permits?
sections.html:
Most of Jasper County's recent growth sits around Hardeeville, where the city grew from 2,952 residents in 2010 to 7,473 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 16,459. New planned communities along U.S. 278 and Argent Boulevard, including Sun City Hilton Head, drove much of it. The median age in Hardeeville in 2020 was 60.4.

  • I-95 has exits 5 and 8 in Hardeeville, and U.S. 17, 278, 321, SC 46 and SC 170 also serve the area.
  • Palmetto Breeze provides public transit, and the county's Ridgeland airport is listed as 3J1.
  • Electric service comes from Palmetto Electric Cooperative or Dominion Energy, and water and sewer from the Town of Ridgeland or the Beaufort-Jasper Water and Sewer Authority.
  • Schools named by the county include Hardeeville Elementary, Hardeeville Junior and Senior High, Ridgeland Elementary and Ridgeland Secondary Academy of Excellence.

Roof replacement, additions, electrical, plumbing and heating work all need a Jasper County building permit, so ask whether past work on your house was permitted. The Planning and Building office is at 358 Third Avenue, Room 202, phone (843) 717-3650. Reports of code violations go to (843) 547-8290.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Jasper County?
sections.html:
The Jasper County Register of Deeds lists a $15 recording fee for a deed, plus documentary stamps where they apply. Fees were set as flat amounts as of August 1, 2019, so call (843) 717-3615 for current numbers.

  • Mortgage: $25.
  • Plat: $25.
  • Release, satisfaction or discharge: $10.
  • Easement: $25 plus stamps.

The state rate for the deed fee is $1.85 per $500 of value under Title 12, Chapter 24. The county's register page gives the address as 358 Third Avenue and mailing as a P.O. Box, with different box numbers in different spots, so confirm that too.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Jasper County, SC?
faqs.a: January 15 is the last penalty-free day. Jasper County's Treasurer lists a 3 percent penalty from January 16, 10 percent from February 2 and 15 percent from March 17, with files going to the Delinquent Tax Collector after that.

faqs.q: Who do I call to appeal my Jasper County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor appeals line at (843) 717-3620. Written objection is due within 90 days of the assessment notice mailing date.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Jasper County property after a tax sale?
faqs.a: You have 12 months from the sale date. The owner, a mortgage company or a grantee may pay the delinquent taxes and sale costs to regain ownership.

faqs.q: When is the Jasper County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county says it is held on the first Monday of November at 358 Third Avenue in Ridgeland. The advertisement lists the exact date and time.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Jasper County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes due are normally settled from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the Treasurer or Tax Collector for a payoff figure before you set a date.
